Desktop RF Analysis Report

WeLink Arizona BEAD - Terrain & Fresnel Zone Clearance Assessment
SRTM1 (30m) DEM | CBRS 3.625 GHz + 6 GHz | 30m AGL BN / 5m AGL RNm
Date: April 5, 2026 | Engineer: Claude (reviewed by Sam Curtis, P.E.)
Bottom Line: Desktop terrain analysis of the four highest-priority Neil elevation sites shows that Luke AFB Water Tower and ASR 1250965 have strong Fresnel clearance through 10km (90%+ pass rate in most bands), making them strong candidates for field validation. Phoenix Sonoran Preserve degrades significantly beyond 5km due to terrain ridgelines to the south and east, and Bunker Peak has directional blockage to the east/southeast from adjacent ridgelines. The CBRS link budget supports 10km paths in free space, but margin is thin (+0.9 dB) and assumes Cat B CBSD EIRP with beamforming. 6 GHz fades beyond 5km, confirming it serves as a capacity band at closer range, not the reach band. Recommendation: Proceed with field validation at Luke AFB Water Tower and ASR 1250965 first. Defer Phoenix Sonoran Preserve and Bunker Peak until directional sector plans account for the terrain-obstructed azimuths.

2. Fresnel Zone Clearance Analysis

Methodology: For each site, 16 radial bearings were sampled at 5 distance bands (2, 4, 6, 8, 10 km). At each sample point, a terrain profile was extracted from the SRTM1 DEM and first Fresnel zone clearance was calculated at CBRS 3.625 GHz. BN height: 30m AGL. RNm height: 5m AGL (rooftop).

Classification: CLEAR LOS = 100%+ F1 clearance | nLOS ADEQUATE = 60-100% F1 | MARGINAL = 0-60% F1 | OBSTRUCTED = terrain blocks LOS

Green = Clear LOS (100%+ F1), Blue = nLOS Adequate (60-100%), Orange = Marginal (0-60%), Red = Obstructed (LOS blocked)

Luke AFB Water Tower

Verdict: STRONG CANDIDATE

Excellent clearance through 10km. Only 2 of 79 paths obstructed (both to NW toward White Tank Mountains). 94% pass rate at 8-10km band. The water tower structure adds significant height advantage. Recommend as the #1 field validation site.

Key Risks: NW sector toward White Tanks is blocked. Luke AFB access requires military coordination.

Phoenix Sonoran Preserve

Verdict: DIRECTIONAL ISSUES

Strong clearance to the west and north, but significant terrain obstruction to the south and east from McDowell Mountain ridgelines. At 622m AMSL this is the highest site, but the surrounding terrain creates blind spots. 33% pass rate at 8-10km is concerning. Most BSLs are to the south/southwest.

Key Risks: Ridgeline obstructions on SE/S azimuths where most BSLs are located. High site but surrounded by terrain. May need sector plan that avoids blocked directions.

ASR 1250965

Verdict: STRONG CANDIDATE

Very strong clearance in all directions through 10km. 100% pass rate through 8km, 82% at 8-10km. Existing ASR tower provides proven structural platform. Moderate elevation (370m) but flat surrounding terrain means fewer obstructions than higher mountain sites.

Bunker Peak

Verdict: DIRECTIONAL ISSUES

Strong clearance to the west and south, but severe blockage to the east and southeast from adjacent ridgelines. The 62% pass rate at 3-5km is a red flag - obstructions start close in. At 481m this is an elevated site but the surrounding Hieroglyphic Mountains create deep shadow zones.

Interpretation: CBRS provides the reach (viable to ~10km with thin margin). 6 GHz provides capacity boost at closer range (<5km). The RNm spec aggregates both bands (160 MHz total), using CBRS for the distant BSLs and 6 GHz for throughput uplift where signal allows. This is consistent with Tarana's stated design intent for the BN-RNm product.

Caveat: This is a simplified FSPL model. The Tarana G2 uses proprietary adaptive beamforming and DSP that performs better than classical link budget in nLOS conditions. The FSPL analysis provides a conservative lower bound. Actual system performance should exceed these numbers, particularly in nLOS conditions where Tarana's technology differentiates.

Desktop Analysis Limitations

This analysis identifies terrain-level obstructions only. It does not account for:

FactorImpactMitigation
Buildings / structuresnLOS degradation in urban areasTarana DSP handles; field test confirms
Vegetation / tree canopy3-10 dB additional loss at CBRSPhoenix desert = minimal tree canopy
Clutter (signs, power lines)Diffraction / scatterCaptured in field test measurements
MultipathCan help or hurt at CBRSTarana beamforming mitigates
Actual antenna heightWater towers may be 40-60m AGL vs 30m modeledWould improve results

Phoenix metro's flat desert terrain and low vegetation make the SRTM terrain model more predictive here than in forested or heavily built environments.

Proposed Validation Sequence

Gate 1 (this report): Desktop terrain analysis eliminates dry wells. COMPLETE

Gate 2: Drone LOS survey at Bunker Peak and Phoenix Sonoran Preserve. Photo/video from planned antenna height confirming actual propagation environment. Cost: ~$2-3K per site.

Gate 3: Drive test at ASR 1250965 and Luke AFB Water Tower per the MOP. This validates the 10km RNm range assumption with actual hardware.

Gate 4: If Gate 3 confirms 8-10km range, extend drive testing to remaining Neil sites that passed desktop screening.
